name: Magpie
summary: McMaster Rocketry's first scientific payload: an SRAD fracture-test module that flew on Osiris to characterize how epoxy test samples fracture under real flight loads, groundwork for a self-healing polymer payload.
detail:
Self-healing polymers could address critical durability needs in reusable launch vehicles, which face extreme acceleration, intense aerodynamic loads, and repeated thermal cycling. Magpie is the first step toward flying one: it characterizes the fracture mechanism of TDCB epoxy test articles and how a sounding-rocket launch environment affects it. That baseline feeds this year's payload, which aims to fly a self-healing polymer.

Magpie carries three test articles. A linear actuator on a Delrin guide loads the samples under tension while SRAD boards record strain, temperature, and pressure data over CAN bus. The module is fully passive once initiated: no pyrotechnics, pressurized parts, or active deployment that could affect the vehicle. It flew on Osiris and won first place in the Payload Challenge at Launch Canada 2026.

blocks.heading: The Magpie bus.
blocks.body: SLS nylon mounts house three SRAD PCBs and four 14500 Li-ion cells. A CNC-machined 6061-aluminum bus forms the skeleton: a ring-and-rod frame that carries the experiment modules and electronics stack, secured to the payload bay via a U-bolt on the top plate.

parts.alt: CAD render of the Magpie top bulkhead with U-bolt mount and payload-bay interface.
CAD render of the Magpie bottom bulkhead ring with six strut mounting tabs.
CAD render of a machined 6061 aluminum strut with countersunk mounting holes.

blocks.heading: Fracture test modules.
blocks.body: TDCB samples are cast in custom SLA 3D-printed molds from 105 epoxy resin. Each fracture test module combines machined 6061 aluminum (baseplate, mount, couplers), a Delrin guide, an Actuonix P8-10-165-3-ST linear actuator (165:1 gear ratio, 10 mm stroke), and a DMYH-113 bidirectional 10 kg load cell.
blocks.imageAlt: CAD render of a fracture test module with actuator, load cell, and coloured fixture blocks.

render.alt: Full CAD render of the Magpie assembly: aluminum strut frame, three experiment modules, and stacked SRAD electronics.

procedure: Pre-flight: begin the fracture test; upon full fracture, return actuators to zero-load positions.
Post-flight: evaluate sample and FTM condition; compare logged data with bench tests.
Post-competition: run new test samples in the flown FTMs to gauge how flight affected hardware performance.

name: Sparrow
summary: A 360-degree camera paired with a recovery beacon, flown on Nimbus. Won first place in the Payload Challenge at Launch Canada 2025.
detail: Sparrow paired a 360-degree camera with a recovery beacon: designed to capture full-flight footage in every direction, plus a way to find the airframe faster after it lands. It flew on Nimbus and won first place in the Payload Challenge at Launch Canada 2025, though its camera data was not recovered after the flight.
